bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the reference executable

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The reference `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version

- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the reference executable (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)

### 3. How the reference executable may be observed

through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the reference `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

.\" This manpage was written by Carla Valenti <valenti.karla@gmail.com>
.\" and Christian Giessen <cgie@informatik.uni-kiel.de> for tty-clock.
.\" In details the command line options displayed by tty-clock -h as
.\" well as the keyboard commands.
.TH "TTY-CLOCK" "1" "October 2013" "" "User Commands"
.SH "NAME"
.LP
tty\-clock \- a terminal digital clock
.SH "SYNOPSIS"
.LP
\fBtty\-clock [\-iuvsScbtrahDBxn] [\-C [\fI0\-7\fB]] [\-f \fIformat\fB] [\-d \fIdelay\fB] [\-a \fInsdelay\fB] \fB[\-T \fItty\fB]\fR
.SH "DESCRIPTION"
.LP
\fItty\-clock\fR displays a simple digital clock on the terminal. Invoked without options
it will display the clock on the upper left corner of the screen on the terminal it was
executed from.
.SH "COMMANDS"
.LP
\fItty\-clock\fR accepts a number of runtime keyboard commands, upper and lower case characters are
treated identically.
.TP
K,J,H,L
vi\-style movement commands to set the position of the displayed clock.
These commands have no effect when the \fBcentered\fR option is set.
.TP
[0\-7]
Select a different color for displaying the clock.
.TP
B
Toggles between bold and normal colors.
.TP
X
Toggles displaying a box around the clock. This option is disabled by default.
.TP
C
Toggle the clock's position to \fBcentered\fR.
When set the movement commands are disabled.
.TP
R
Set the clock to \fBrebound\fR along the edges of the terminal.
.TP
S
Display seconds.
.TP
T
Switch time output to the 12\-hour format.
.TP
Q
Quit.
.SH "OPTIONS"
.LP
.TP
\fB\-s\fR
Show seconds.
.TP
\fB\-S\fR
Screensaver mode. tty\-clock terminates when any key is pressed.
.TP
\fB\-x\fR
Show box.
.TP
\fB\-c\fR
Set the clock at the center of the terminal.
.TP
\fB\-C\fR \fI[0\-7]\fR
Set the clock color.
.TP
\fB\-b\fR
Use bold colors.
.TP
\fB\-t\fR
Set the hour in 12h format.
.TP
\fB\-u\fR
Use UTC time.
.TP
\fB\-T\fR \fItty\fR
Display the clock on the given \fItty\fR. \fItty\fR must be
a valid character device to which the user has rw access permissions.
(See \fBEXAMPLES\fR)
.TP
\fB\-r\fR
Do rebound the clock.
.TP
\fB\-f\fR \fIformat\fR
Set the date format as described in \fBstrftime(3)\fR.
.TP
\fB\-n\fR
Do not quit the program when the Q key is pressed (or when any
key is pressed while in \fBScreensaver\fR mode). A signal must
be sent to \fItty\-clock\fR in order to terminate its execution. (See \fBEXAMPLES\fR)
.TP
\fB\-v\fR
Show tty\-clock version.
.TP
\fB\-i\fR
Show some info about tty\-clock.
.TP
\fB\-h\fR
Show usage information.
.TP
\fB\-D\fR
Hide the date.
.TP
\fB\-B\fR
Enable blinking colon.
.TP
\fB\-d\fR \fIdelay\fR
Set the delay (in seconds) between two redraws of the clock. Default 1s.
.TP
\fB\-a\fR \fInsdelay\fR
Additional delay (in nanoseconds) between two redraws of the clock. Default 0ns.
.SH "EXAMPLES"
.LP
To invoke
.I tty\-clock
in screensaver mode with the clock display set to rebound and the update
delay set to 1/10th of a second (10 FPS):
.IP
$ tty\-clock \-Sra 100000000 \-d 0
.LP
The following example arranges for \fItty\-clock\fR to be displayed
indefinitely on one of the Virtual Terminals on a Linux system
at boot time using an
.B inittab(5)
entry:
.IP
# /etc/inittab:
.br
9:2345:respawn:/usr/bin/tty\-clock \-c \-n \-T /dev/tty9
.LP

import subprocess, sys, time, os, re
def cap(name, args, w=80, h=24, wait=1.2, keys=[], extra_env="", kill_after=True):
    sess=f"p{name}"
    subprocess.run(["tmux","kill-session","-t",sess], capture_output=True)
    cmd=f"{extra_env} TERM=xterm-256color /workspace/executable {args}"
    subprocess.run(["tmux","new-session","-d","-s",sess,"-x",str(w),"-y",str(h),cmd], check=True)
    time.sleep(wait)
    for k in keys:
        # k could be tuple
        subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t",sess]+ (k if isinstance(k,list) else [k]))
        time.sleep(0.35)
    out=subprocess.run(["tmux","capture-pane","-t",sess,"-p","-e"], capture_output=True, text=True)
    txt=out.stdout
    # parse
    print(f"=== {name} args={args!r} keys={keys} alive? ", end="")
    alive=subprocess.run(["tmux","has-session","-t",sess], capture_output=True).returncode==0
    print(alive)
    rows=[]
    for line in txt.split("\n"):
        # strip? show grid
        # Replace ANSI bg codes: we need to interpret.
        # produce representation: '.' blank, '#' if in bg color 4x
        s=line
        # parse CSI
        out_chars=[]
        colors=[]
        cur_bg=None; cur_fg=None; bold=False
        i=0
        while i < len(s):
            if s[i]=='\x1b' and i+1<len(s) and s[i+1]=='[':
                j=s.find('m',i)
                code=s[i+2:j]
                parts=code.split(';') if code else []
                for p in parts:
                    try: n=int(p) if p else 0
                    except: n=0
                    if 40<=n<=49: cur_bg=n
                    elif 30<=n<=39: cur_fg=n
                    elif n==1: bold=True
                    elif n==0: cur_bg=None; cur_fg=None; bold=False
                i=j+1
                continue
            else:
                ch=s[i]
                out_chars.append(ch)

        while i<len(line):
            if line[i]=='\x1b' and line[i+1]=='[':
                j=line.find('m',i); code=line[i+2:j]
                for p in code.split(';'):
                    n=int(p) if p else 0
                    if 40<=n<=49: bg=n
                    elif 30<=n<=39: fg=n
                    elif n==1: bold=True
                    elif n==0: bg=fg=None; bold=False
                i=j+1; continue
            chars.append(line[i]); cols.append((bg,fg,bold)); i+=1
        # pad to w
        grid=''.join('#' if (bg is not None and bg!=49) else (ch if ch!=' ' else '.') for ch,(bg,fg,b) in zip(chars,cols))
        rows.append((grid.ljust(w,'.'), ''.join(chars).ljust(w,' '), cols))
    return rows

# Interpret nanosleep EINVAL cases: tv_sec=-1? or tv_nsec out of range gives error -> returns immediately? Let's think:

/* Handle one key.  Returns 0 if the program should exit. */
static int handle_key(int key) {
    if (key == ERR) return 1;

    if (key == KEY_RESIZE) {
        layout_dirty = 1;
        return 1;
    }

    /* Arrow keys behave exactly like the vi movement keys. */
    if (key == KEY_LEFT) key = 'h';
    else if (key == KEY_DOWN) key = 'j';
    else if (key == KEY_UP) key = 'k';
    else if (key == KEY_RIGHT) key = 'l';

    switch (key) {
        case 'q':
        case 'Q':
            return ttyclock.option.dontquit ? 1 : 0;

        case 'h': case 'H':
            if (!ttyclock.option.center && ttyclock.x > 0) {
                ttyclock.x--;
                move_windows();
                if (ttyclock.option.rebound) rebound_step();
            }
            break;
        case 'l': case 'L': {
            int xm = xmax_pos();
            if (!ttyclock.option.center && xm >= 0 && ttyclock.x < xm) {
                ttyclock.x++;
                move_windows();
                if (ttyclock.option.rebound) rebound_step();
            }
            break;
        }
        case 'k': case 'K':
            if (!ttyclock.option.center && ttyclock.y > 0) {
                ttyclock.y--;
                move_windows();
                if (ttyclock.option.rebound) rebound_step();
            }
            break;
        case 'j': case 'J': {
            int ym = ymax_pos();
            if (!ttyclock.option.center && ym >= 0 && ttyclock.y < ym) {
                ttyclock.y++;
                move_windows();
                if (ttyclock.option.rebound) rebound_step();
            }
            break;
        }

        case 'c': case 'C':
            ttyclock.option.center = !ttyclock.option.center;
            if (ttyclock.option.center) ttyclock.option.rebound = 0;
            layout_dirty = 1;
            break;

        case 'x': case 'X':
            ttyclock.option.box = !ttyclock.option.box;
            if (ttyclock.option.box) { ttyclock.moved = 0; ttyclock.box_dirty = 1; }
            if (ttyclock.option.box && ttyclock.option.hide_date &&
                ttyclock.datewin) {
                box(ttyclock.datewin, 0, 0);
                wrefresh(ttyclock.datewin);
            }
            if (!ttyclock.option.box) {
                werase(stdscr);
                wrefresh(stdscr);
                if (ttyclock.clockwin) {
                    werase(ttyclock.clockwin);
                    touchwin(ttyclock.clockwin);
                }
                if (ttyclock.datewin) {
                    werase(ttyclock.datewin);
                    touchwin(ttyclock.datewin);
                }
            }
            break;

        case 'b': case 'B':
            ttyclock.option.bold = !ttyclock.option.bold;
            /* Existing digit cells keep their old attributes in the
             * reference until redrawn; ncurses repaints changed
             * cells on the next refresh the same way here. */
            break;

        case 'r': case 'R':
            ttyclock.option.rebound = !ttyclock.option.rebound;
            if (ttyclock.option.rebound && !ttyclock.option.center)
                rebound_step();
            break;

        case 's': case 'S': {
            ttyclock.option.second = !ttyclock.option.second;
            if (ttyclock.option.second && !ttyclock.option.center) {
                int neww = 54;
                int xm = getmaxx(stdscr) - neww;
                if (xm >= 0 && ttyclock.x >= xm) ttyclock.x = xm - 1;
                if (ttyclock.x < 0) ttyclock.x = 0;
            }
            layout_dirty = 1;
            break;
        }

        case 't': case 'T':
            ttyclock.option.twelve = !ttyclock.option.twelve;
            layout_dirty = 1;
            break;

        case '0': case '1': case '2': case '3':
        case '4': case '5': case '6': case '7':
            if (ttyclock.option.screensaver) {
                /* Inside the screensaver only the colour keys are
                 * acted on.  Queue the colour change so it takes
                 * effect two redraws from now. */
                extern void queue_color(int);
                queue_color(key - '0');
            } else {
                ttyclock.option.color = key - '0';
                init_pair(1, -1, ttyclock.option.color);
                init_pair(2, ttyclock.option.color, -1);
            }
            break;

        default:
            break;
    }
    return 1;
}

/* Screensaver colour changes are delayed by two cycles. */
static int delayed_color = -1;
static int delayed_color_age = 0;
void queue_color(int c) {
    delayed_color = c;
    delayed_color_age = 0;
}
static void age_delayed_color(void) {
    if (delayed_color < 0) return;
    if (++delayed_color_age >= 2) {
        ttyclock.option.color = delayed_color;
        init_pair(1, -1, ttyclock.option.color);
        init_pair(2, ttyclock.option.color, -1);
        delayed_color = -1;
    }
}

static void rebound_step(void) {
    int xm = xmax_pos();
    int ym = ymax_pos();
    int nx = ttyclock.x + xdir;
    if (xm >= 0 && nx > xm) { xdir = -xdir; nx = ttyclock.x + xdir; }
    else if (nx < 0) { xdir = -xdir; nx = ttyclock.x + xdir; }
    if (xm >= 0) ttyclock.x = nx;
    int ny = ttyclock.y + ydir;
    if (ym >= 0 && ny > ym) { ydir = -ydir; ny = ttyclock.y + ydir; }
    else if (ny < 0) { ydir = -ydir; ny = ttyclock.y + ydir; }
    if (ym >= 0) ttyclock.y = ny;
    move_windows();
}

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
    memset(&ttyclock, 0, sizeof ttyclock);
    ttyclock.option.color = 2;
    ttyclock.option.format = "%Y-%m-%d";
    ttyclock.option.delay = 1;
    ttyclock.option.nsdelay = 0;

    int c;
    while ((c = getopt(argc, argv, "iuvsScbtrhDBxnC:f:d:a:T:")) != -1) {
        switch (c) {
            case 's': ttyclock.option.second = 1; break;
            case 'S': ttyclock.option.screensaver = 1; break;
            case 'x': ttyclock.option.box = 1; break;
            case 'c': ttyclock.option.center = 1; break;
            case 'C': {
                int col = atoi(optarg);
                if (col >= 0 && col <= 7) ttyclock.option.color = col;
                break;
            }
            case 'b': ttyclock.option.bold = 1; break;
            case 't': ttyclock.option.twelve = 1; break;
            case 'u': ttyclock.option.utc = 1; break;
            case 'T': {
                struct stat st;
                if (stat(optarg, &st) != 0) {
                    fprintf(stderr,
                        "tty-clock: error: couldn't stat '%s': %s.\n",
                        optarg, strerror(errno));
                    exit(1);
                }
                if (!S_ISCHR(st.st_mode)) {
                    fprintf(stderr,
                        "tty-clock: error: '%s' doesn't appear to be a character device.\n",
                        optarg);
                    exit(1);
                }
                ttyclock.option.tty = optarg;
                break;
            }
            case 'r': ttyclock.option.rebound = 1; break;
            case 'f': ttyclock.option.format = optarg; break;
            case 'n': ttyclock.option.dontquit = 1; break;
            case 'v':
                printf("TTY-Clock 2 \302\251 devel version\n");
                return 0;
            case 'i':
                printf("TTY-Clock 2 \302\251 by Martin Duquesnoy (xorg62@gmail.com), Grey (grey@greytheory.net)\n");
                return 0;
            case 'h': usage(); break;
            case 'D': ttyclock.option.hide_date = 1; break;
            case 'B': ttyclock.option.blink = 1; break;
            case 'd': ttyclock.option.delay = atol(optarg); break;
            case 'a': ttyclock.option.nsdelay = atol(optarg); break;
            default: usage(); break;
        }
    }

    struct sigaction sa;
    memset(&sa, 0, sizeof sa);
    sa.sa_handler = sig_handler;
    sigemptyset(&sa.sa_mask);
    sa.sa_flags = 0;
    sigaction(SIGINT, &sa, NULL);
    sigaction(SIGTERM, &sa, NULL);

    init();
    ttyclock.running = 1;

    /* First position: rebounding clocks step once before drawing. */
    if (ttyclock.option.rebound && !ttyclock.option.center)
        rebound_step();
    if (ttyclock.option.center ||
        !(ttyclock.option.rebound))
        move_windows();
    draw_all();
    ttyclock.moved = 0;

    while (ttyclock.running) {
        int input_ready = wait_delay();
        if (sigflag) break;

        if (ttyclock.option.screensaver) {
            int handled_now = ERR;
            if (input_ready && pending != ERR) {
                handled_now = pending;
                pending = ERR;
                if (handled_now == KEY_RESIZE) {
                    layout_dirty = 1;
                } else if (handled_now >= '0' && handled_now <= '7') {
                    if (!handle_key(handled_now)) break;
                }
                if (handled_now != KEY_RESIZE &&
                    !ttyclock.option.dontquit)
                    break;
                if (handled_now != KEY_RESIZE)
                    ss_pending = handled_now;
            }
            age_delayed_color();
            if (ttyclock.option.rebound && !ttyclock.option.center)
                rebound_step();
            if (layout_dirty) {
                layout_dirty = 0;
                deinit();
                /* endwin()+refresh picks up the new terminal size */
                endwin();
                refresh();
                init();
                ttyclock.moved = 1;
            }
            draw_all();
            ttyclock.moved = 0;
            if (ss_pending != ERR && ss_pending != KEY_RESIZE &&
                !ttyclock.option.dontquit) {
                /* The screensaver notices the key one cycle after
                 * it was read: exit after the following redraw. */
                if (handled_now == ERR || handled_now != ss_pending) {
                    ss_pending = ERR;
                    break;
                }
                /* handled this very cycle: give it one more cycle */
            }
            if (ss_pending != ERR && handled_now == ERR &&
                !ttyclock.option.dontquit) {
                ss_pending = ERR;
                break;
            }
            continue;
        }

        /* Normal mode.  Always ask curses for a key so that
         * synthesized keys such as KEY_RESIZE are picked up.
         * Movement is applied on top of the position the clock
         * is about to rebound to. */

        if (ttyclock.option.rebound && !ttyclock.option.center)
            rebound_step();
        {
            nodelay(stdscr, TRUE);
            key = getch();
            nodelay(stdscr, FALSE);
            if (key != ERR && !handle_key(key)) ttyclock.running = 0;
        }
        (void)input_ready;
        if (ttyclock.x != x0 || ttyclock.y != y0) {
            werase(stdscr);
            wrefresh(stdscr);
            if (ttyclock.clockwin) touchwin(ttyclock.clockwin);
        }
        if (layout_dirty) {
            layout_dirty = 0;
            deinit();
            endwin();
            refresh();
            init();
            ttyclock.moved = 1;
        }
        draw_all();
        ttyclock.moved = 0;
    }

    /* Teardown in the order that just calls endwin: curses restores
     * the terminal (cursor, alternate screen, keypad mode). */
    deinit();
    endwin();
    if (ttyclock.ttyscr) delscreen(ttyclock.ttyscr);
    return 0;
}

    wattroff(ttyclock.clockwin, 1 << 19);
    int i, j;
    for (i = 0; i < 5; i++) {
        for (j = 0; j < 3; j++) {
            int on = digits[10][i * 3 + j];
            if (ttyclock.option.blink && (ttyclock.tim.tm_sec % 2) == 0)
                on = 0;
            if (on) {
                wattron(ttyclock.clockwin, COLOR_PAIR(1));
                mvwaddstr(ttyclock.clockwin, y + i, x + j * 2, "  ");
                wattroff(ttyclock.clockwin, COLOR_PAIR(1));
            } else {
                mvwaddstr(ttyclock.clockwin, y + i, x + j * 2, "  ");
            }
        }
    }
}

void draw_clock(void) {
    int hour = ttyclock.tim.tm_hour;
    int minute = ttyclock.tim.tm_min;
    int second = ttyclock.tim.tm_sec;
    if (ttyclock.option.twelve) {
        if (hour > 12) hour -= 12;
        else if (hour == 0) hour = 12;
    }
    print_digit(hour / 10, 1, 1);
    print_digit(hour % 10, 8, 1);
    print_colon(14, 1);
    print_digit(minute / 10, 20, 1);
    print_digit(minute % 10, 27, 1);
    if (ttyclock.option.second) {
        print_colon(33, 1);
        print_digit(second / 10, 39, 1);
        print_digit(second % 10, 46, 1);
    }
}

void print_digit(int digit, int x, int y) {
    if (ttyclock.option.bold) wattron(ttyclock.clockwin, 1 << 19);
    int i, j;
    for (i = 0; i < 5; i++) {
        for (j = 0; j < 3; j++) {
            int cx = x + j * 2;
            int on = digits[digit][i * 3 + j];
            if (digit == 10 && ttyclock.option.blink &&
                (ttyclock.tim.tm_sec % 2) == 0)
                on = 0;
            if (on) {
                wattron(ttyclock.clockwin, COLOR_PAIR(1));
                mvwaddstr(ttyclock.clockwin, y + i, cx, "  ");
                wattroff(ttyclock.clockwin, COLOR_PAIR(1));
            } else {
                mvwaddstr(ttyclock.clockwin, y + i, cx, "  ");
            }
        }
    }
    wrefresh(ttyclock.clockwin);
}

void set_box(void) {
    if (ttyclock.datewin && !ttyclock.option.hide_date) {
        box(ttyclock.datewin, 0, 0);
        wrefresh(ttyclock.datewin);
    }
    if (ttyclock.clockwin) {
        box(ttyclock.clockwin, 0, 0);
        wrefresh(ttyclock.clockwin);
    }
    ttyclock.box_dirty = 0;
}

int key_event(void) { return 0; }

Implementation committed. Summary of the work:

**Approach:** Black-box reimplementation of tty-clock in C/ncursesw (`src/main.c`, `src/ttyclock.c`, `src/ttyclock.h`, `compile.sh`). Behavior was probed via tmux screen captures under an LD_PRELOAD-faked clock (for deterministic times), raw pty byte comparisons, and extensive CLI differential testing against the reference.

**Matched behavior includes:**
- Big-digit (3×5, two cells per pixel) clock in a 35×7 (54 with seconds) window, separate date window, per-digit refreshes, colon rendered inside the next digit's refresh
- All flags (`-s -S -x -c -C -b -t -u -T -r -f -n -v -i -h -D -B -d -a`) with exact usage/version/info bytes, getopt ordering of `-v/-i/-h`/errors, and `-T`'s parse-time stat/char-device validation messages
- Runtime keys (hjkl + arrows, q, c, x, b, r, s, t, 0–7), movement/rebound bounds, centering formulas, box joins, the phantom date-box after `x` with `-D`
- Quirks: "bold" digits use the raw attribute bit (emitted as blink), blinking colon follows seconds parity, screensaver keys only take effect after the full redraw delay (only color keys are honored, delayed), invalid/negative/huge `-d`/`-a` timing behavior, `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` → clean exit 0, stdin-EOF spin behavior, and the identical `ttyclock.c:53: init` assertion abort for `-T` with an unopenable terminal

**Verification:** ~150 differential tmux cases (times, sizes, keys, resizes, signals, screensaver, formats, timezones, TERM variants), byte-identical raw pty streams for common modes (`-D`, `-s -D`, `-x`, exit-on-q), plus a fresh-clone `compile.sh` build test. Remaining known diffs are single-cell border artifacts in a few exotic small sizes (h≤10 with `-x -c`) and a 2-byte cursor-move choice in raw streams with a date.
